question: What is the learning rate doing in gradient descent, conceptually and mathematically?
direct_answer: It scales the step size, controlling how far parameters move in the gradient direction at each update.
expanded_answer: Mathematically, the learning rate multiplies the gradient before the update, so it acts like a step-size parameter. Conceptually, it controls how aggressively the optimizer follows the local slope. A small learning rate makes cautious, slow updates; a large learning rate makes larger jumps that may accelerate progress or destabilize training.
key_points: Learning rate scales the update size
Applies to every gradient step in basic GD
common_wrong_ideas: A higher learning rate always trains better
Learning rate changes the gradient itself
Learning rate only matters at the start of training
